originalTitle: China advises its citizens to leave Taiwan ally Eswatini over 'security risks'
title: News Flash! What's Happening in Our Friend Eswatini?
content:
Hello, Super Reporters and Friends!

Hello, amazing friends from all over Africa! It's your friendly news reporter here, ready to share some interesting news from our very own continent. We are going to talk about a beautiful country called Eswatini. It's a special place with kind people and lots of stories. Today, we have some news about Eswatini and a far-away country called China. It's a bit like when you have different friends at school, and sometimes things can get a little tricky. But don't worry, we will explain everything in simple words!

Meet Eswatini: The Kingdom of Fun!

Let's start with Eswatini! Do you know where Eswatini is? It's a lovely country right here in Africa. It's a small place, but it has a very big heart. Eswatini used to be called Swaziland. But now it has a new, proud name: Eswatini! It means 'place of the Swazi' people. It is a kingdom, which means it has a king! How cool is that? The people of Eswatini are known for their warm smiles and rich culture. They love to dance and sing, and their festivals are very colourful. Did you know? Eswatini is one of the smallest countries in Africa, but it's full of beautiful mountains and lovely valleys! It's also famous for its amazing wildlife, like elephants and rhinos.

Countries Are Like Friends

Imagine you have many friends at school. Countries also have friends! These friends are other countries. When countries are friends, they talk to each other. They help each other. They trade things, like food or toys, or even ideas! This is called having 'diplomatic relations'. It means they have a special way of talking and working together. Some countries are very close friends, and some are just friendly neighbours. Just like in your classroom, right? Did you know? Having friends helps countries learn from each other and make the world a better place for everyone!

China and Taiwan: A Family Story

Now, let's meet China and Taiwan. China is a HUGE country. It has more people than any other country in the whole world! It's a very big and powerful place, far away from Africa. Taiwan is an island, which means it's surrounded by water. It's much smaller than China. Taiwan has its own government and its own way of doing things. China believes that Taiwan is part of *its* country. But Taiwan believes it is a separate country. It's a bit like two family members who have different ideas about things. Because of this, China wants all other countries to be friends with *it*, and not with Taiwan. It's like asking your friends to only play with you, not with your cousin if you're not getting along. Did you know? China is so big that you can find many different types of weather and amazing places there, like the Great Wall of China!

Eswatini's Special Friendship

Here's where Eswatini comes into our story. Eswatini is friends with Taiwan! Yes, Eswatini talks to Taiwan, and they are good friends. This is very special because Eswatini is the *only* country in all of Africa that is friends with Taiwan. All the other countries in Africa are friends with China. So, Eswatini is unique! It has chosen to be friends with Taiwan, even though China might not like that very much. Did you know? There are only about 12 countries in the whole world that are friends with Taiwan. Eswatini is one of them!

China's Message to Its People

Now for the news! China has told its people, who are called 'citizens', to leave Eswatini. They have said, "It's better to come home or go somewhere else for now." Why did China say this? They said it's because of 'security risks'. That sounds like big words, doesn't it? What 'security risks' means is that China thinks it might not be very safe for its people in Eswatini right now. It means there might be some problems or dangers that could make things difficult or even risky for them. So, China wants its own people to be safe. Just like your mom or dad tells you to be careful and stay safe, countries tell their citizens to be safe too. Did you know? People who live in a country are called citizens of that country. We are all citizens of our countries!

Why China is Saying 'Be Careful'

China might be worried because Eswatini is friends with Taiwan. When countries have different friends, sometimes things can get complicated. This can make the situation a bit unstable. China wants to make sure its citizens are not caught in any tricky situations. So, they tell them to leave Eswatini and go to a place where they feel more secure. It's a way for China to protect its people, especially when there are big differences in how countries are friends. Did you know? It's always a good idea to listen to advice about staying safe, no matter where you are!

What This Means for Eswatini and Us

So, what does all this mean? Eswatini is still a beautiful and strong country. Its friendship with Taiwan continues. This news tells us that even far away, things happening between big countries can affect others. But the people of Eswatini continue with their lives, proud of their country. It's important for us to learn about different countries and how they are friends. We hope that everyone, everywhere, stays safe and happy. Did you know? We can all be friends, even if we are from different places and have different ideas! That's all for today's news from Africa, my friends! Keep learning and stay curious!
summary: China has told its people to leave Eswatini, a country in Africa, because Eswatini is friends with Taiwan instead of China, and China wants its citizens to be safe from 'security risks'.
whyMatters: This news is important because it shows how friendships between countries can be tricky, and it highlights Eswatini as the only African country that is friends with Taiwan, making it unique and special.

originalTitle: Guinea's president dismisses 173 soldiers, including coup ally, for desertion
title: Big News from Guinea: President Makes a Big Change!
content:
Hello, Junior Reporters!

Hello, amazing junior reporters from all over Africa! Your friend, News Explorer Nana, is here with some super important news today. We're going on an adventure to a country called Guinea! Guinea is a beautiful country in West Africa. It's full of interesting people and wonderful places. Today, we have some big news about what is happening there with their leader. Sometimes, big leaders make big decisions. Today, we will learn about one such big decision that happened very recently. It's like when your teacher makes a new rule in class, or when your family decides something important together. Let's find out more!

What Happened in Guinea?

Imagine you have a super important job. In Guinea, there are special people called soldiers. Their job is to keep everyone safe. They wear uniforms and are very brave. Recently, the boss of Guinea, who we call the President, made a big announcement. He said that many soldiers would not be able to do their jobs anymore. Wow! That's a lot of people, isn't it? It's like telling almost 200 people to find a new job. That's a very big number! This news is about 173 soldiers. That's more than a hundred, almost two hundred! The President told them that their time as soldiers was finished.

Who are Soldiers?

Soldiers are like superheroes for their country! They train very hard to protect their home and their people. They learn many special skills. They wear special clothes, called uniforms, so everyone knows they are soldiers. Their job is to make sure everyone is safe and that the country's rules are followed. Did you know? Soldiers often help people when there are big problems, like floods or other emergencies! They are not just for fighting, but for helping too! They are very important people in every country. They work hard to keep peace and order. We thank them for their brave work.

What Does 'Dismissed' Mean?

The news said the soldiers were 'dismissed.' What does that big word mean? It means they were told to leave their jobs. It's like when your mom or dad might say, 'Okay, playtime is dismissed, time for dinner!' It means it's over. So, for these soldiers, their job as a soldier was finished. They can't wear their uniforms or do soldier work anymore. It's a very serious thing to be dismissed from a job, especially a very important job like a soldier. Did you know? Sometimes, if you don't follow the rules at school, you might be 'dismissed' from an activity, meaning you can't join in!

What is 'Desertion'?

The President said these soldiers were dismissed because of 'desertion.' That's another big word! Let's make it simple. Desertion means leaving your very important job without asking permission. It's like running away from your responsibilities. Imagine you promised to help your friend clean up, but then you just leave and play without telling them. That would be like desertion from your promise! For soldiers, desertion is a very serious rule to break. Their job is to be there, always, to protect the country. When soldiers desert, it means they left their important post. They did not do their duty. This can make a country less safe. Did you know? In olden times, desertion was seen as a very big crime because it could put many people in danger!

Why Did This Happen?

So, why did the President of Guinea make such a big decision? It's because he wants to be super, super sure that everyone listens to him. He wants to be the main boss, and he wants all the soldiers to follow his lead. He wants to make sure he is strong and in control of the country. When the news says 'consolidate control,' it means the boss wants to make sure everyone understands he is the boss. He wants to make his power very strong. He had help from some people before to become the leader. Now, he wants to be sure that *everyone* trusts him and follows him, not just some. He wants to make sure that his country is running smoothly. For that, everyone needs to be working together and following the leader's plan. Did you know? When a leader 'consolidates control,' it means they are making sure their plans for the country can happen without problems.

Meet Guinea!

Let's learn a little more about Guinea, our amazing country in West Africa! It's not just a place where big news happens. Guinea has beautiful rivers and tall mountains. It's famous for its rich soil and special minerals like bauxite, which is used to make aluminum! The people of Guinea are very warm and friendly. They speak many different languages, but French is also spoken a lot because of its history. The capital city of Guinea is called Conakry. It's a bustling city right by the ocean! Imagine living by the sea! Did you know? Guinea is shaped a bit like a curving boomerang on the map! It shares borders with many other interesting African countries. It is a country with a rich culture, amazing music, and delicious food. We hope for peace and happiness for all our friends in Guinea.

Why is Having a Strong Leader Important?

In any country, having a strong and clear leader is very important. Think of it like a captain of a football team, or the conductor of an orchestra. The leader helps everyone work together. They make the rules, help people solve problems, and guide the country to be its best. When everyone knows who the leader is and follows the rules, the country can grow and become stronger. This helps everyone live happy lives. Sometimes leaders have to make tough decisions, like the President of Guinea did. They do it because they believe it's best for the country and its people. Did you know? A good leader listens to their people and tries to make decisions that help everyone, especially the children! It's a big job to be a country's leader, and they need support to do it well. That's why following rules is important.

What Happens Next?

Now that these soldiers have been dismissed, the President of Guinea will likely choose new soldiers who will follow all the rules. He wants to make sure that everyone working for the country, especially the army, is loyal and dedicated. This makes the country strong. The goal is always to have a peaceful and safe country where everyone can thrive. That means everyone doing their part. We will keep watching the news from Guinea to see what happens next. Our hope is for peace and happiness for everyone there. Did you know? Countries often have special ceremonies when new soldiers join the army, where they promise to protect their country!

Let's Remember Our Friends in Guinea!

So, junior reporters, we learned a lot today about what happened in Guinea. We learned about soldiers, presidents, and big words like 'dismissed' and 'desertion'. It's important to understand what's happening in our big African family. Every country has its own story, and we should always learn more. Let's send our happy thoughts and wishes for peace to all the people in Guinea. May their country be strong and peaceful. Keep being curious, keep asking questions, and keep learning, amazing junior reporters! Until next time!
summary: The President of Guinea told many soldiers to leave their jobs because they did not follow the rules, as he wants to make sure he is the main boss of the country.
whyMatters: This is important because it shows the leader wants everyone in the army to work together and listen to him, so the country can be safe and strong for all its people.

originalTitle: Ex-head of Rwanda's presidential guard dies in jail 12 years after his arrest
title: A Story from Rwanda: An Important Man Passes Away
content:
Hello, my amazing friends! It's your friendly African news reporter here, bringing you a story from our beautiful continent. Today, we're going to talk about something that happened in a country called Rwanda.

Hello, My Friends!

It's so good to be with you all today! I hope you're having a wonderful day, full of smiles and learning. We live in a big, amazing world, and sometimes grown-ups have big stories to share. Today, I want to tell you about a story from a country called Rwanda. It's a little bit sad, but it's important for us to learn about things happening around us.

Where is Rwanda?

Imagine a map of Africa. It's a really big continent, full of different countries, just like your classroom is full of different friends! Rwanda is one of these countries. It's a small, beautiful land in East Africa. People there speak a language called Kinyarwanda, and they love to sing and dance! Did you know? Rwanda is sometimes called "The Land of a Thousand Hills" because it has so many green, rolling hills. It's truly a sight to see!

Who Was This Important Man?

Our story today is about a man who was very important a long time ago in Rwanda. His name was Colonel Tom Byabagamba. Now, "Colonel" is a special title for someone who is a leader in the army. Imagine your school's head boy or head girl, but for a whole group of soldiers! He was once in charge of special soldiers. These soldiers had a very, very important job. They helped to keep the country's leader safe.

What is a Presidential Guard?

You know how your head teacher is very important in your school? Well, a country also has a very important leader called a President. The President helps to make sure everything in the country runs smoothly and that people are happy and safe. The Presidential Guard is like a team of super-strong, super-brave bodyguards for the President. Their job is to protect the President from any danger, just like your parents protect you. Colonel Tom Byabagamba used to be the boss of these special guards. He was a very powerful and important person in the army. Did you know? Presidents in different countries have different names. Sometimes they are called Prime Ministers or Kings! But they all have a big job to lead their people.

What Does "In Jail" Mean?

Sometimes, people do things that are against the rules. In every country, there are laws that help everyone live together nicely and safely. If someone breaks a very important law, they might have to go to a special place called jail, or prison. Jail is a place where people stay if they are found guilty of breaking big rules. It's a place for them to think about what they did and to learn. It's not a happy place, and people often miss their homes and families a lot when they are there. Colonel Tom Byabagamba was in jail.

A Long, Long Time Ago

The news tells us that Colonel Tom Byabagamba was put in jail a very, very long time ago. Can you imagine 12 years? That's a lot of years! If you are in Class 2, you might be about 7 or 8 years old. So, 12 years is even longer than you have been alive! He was arrested, which means the police took him because they thought he did something wrong. And he stayed in jail for all those 12 years. That's a really, really long time to be away from your family and home. Did you know? Our planet Earth takes one whole year to go around the sun one time. So 12 years means Earth went around the sun 12 times while he was in jail!

His Family Missed Him So Much

Now, here is a part of the story that might make you feel a little sad. Colonel Tom Byabagamba has a brother. His brother told some news reporters that his family was not allowed to see him for all those 12 years. Imagine not seeing your brother, sister, mom, or dad for such a long, long time! Families love each other very much. It's a special bond. Not being able to visit or even talk to someone you love for so many years must have been very hard for them. They must have missed him every single day.

A Sad Goodbye

This week, we heard the sad news that Colonel Tom Byabagamba passed away. To "pass away" means that he died. He was still in jail when this happened. This is a very sad event for his family and for the people who knew him. When someone passes away, it means they are no longer alive. We remember them, and we think about their life. It's a time for families to be together and comfort each other. Even though he was in jail, he was still a person with a family who loved him.

Why We Share Stories Like This

It's important to know about what happens in the world, even if some stories are a little bit sad. Stories like this remind us how important it is for families to be together and to care for each other. It also reminds us that leaders have very big jobs, and sometimes things can be very complicated. We always hope for a world where everyone can live happily and safely with their loved ones. Keep being kind, keep learning, and remember that we are all part of one big African family, and a big world family too! Thank you for listening, my dear friends.
summary: A man who used to be an important soldier in Rwanda died in jail after being there for 12 years, and his family said they could not visit him during that time.
whyMatters: This story helps us understand that even important people can be in difficult situations, and it reminds us how much families miss each other when they are apart.
